dealer.description_hero: In 2020, home delivery was disrupted by new competitors. This pushed Albert Heijn to invest in its delivery service with a new proposition AH Compact. This free service aimed to deliver a selection of people's favorite products. (*Your daily groceries delivered for free)
dealer.section_problem_statement: How to attract smaller households to order their groceries online?
dealer.context_user_desc: We will target smaller households with a lower income, young and old, in need of essential groceries for the week. They will be able to login with their Albert Heijn account and we will deliver them at their earliest convenience.
dealer.context_proposition_desc: A standalone App proposing a smaller assortment of essential products. Users will be able to order their usual products within a few clicks with free delivery, while benefiting from all the loyalty programs of the brand.
dealer.context_enabler_desc: Flutter is an open-source UI software development kit created by Google that can generate iOS and Android applications from a single codebase. This will support our squad to stay flexible, and experiment often.
dealer.section_key_results_desc_01: After 1 year, between the MVP and the last version.
dealer.section_key_results_desc_02: In the last year, we multiplied our user base by 2.
dealer.section_key_results_desc_03: through user research and various AB tests.
dealer.section_key_results_desc_04: We expanded our service from 3 to 16 cities.
dealer.section_context_desc: 2020 — Online grocery is booming, with fierce competition (Gorilla, xxx). This pushed Albert Heijn (dutch’s first supermarket) to invest massively in fast delivery.
dealer.section_ambition_desc: Our objective is to make our service as simpler and relevant as possible. Customers create favourite lists to fill their next order faster. Over time, by learning through our customer's previous purchases, and offering an experience based on their preferences and routines, their grocery order will get easier every single time.
dealer.section_research_desc: User research, user interviews, App stores screening and analytics study was an integral part of the process.
dealer.section_feedback_01: Users first look at discounts before to browse through the rest of the assortment.
dealer.section_feedback_02: Campaigns/Banners are overlooked. Users are generally not interested in our content
dealer.section_feedback_03: Some users are willing to try new products, but the app doesn't highlight any.
dealer.section_feedback_04: Both the conversion and the amount of users are stagnating.
dealer.section_improvement_01: Highlight the discounts of the week with larger banners, more engaging.
dealer.section_improvement_02: Together with the content team, we've adapted the visuals to make them more appealing (MVP)
dealer.section_improvement_03: A 'new product' section has been added to the assortiment page. Conversion increased
dealer.section_improvement_04: Introduced the 'Invite a friend' feature, including a special discount
dealer.section_transition_desc: The App transitioned from a large to a small palette of color to align with the main brand and support the simple to use feeling. Our team also implemented some large features such as 'Invite a friend', a Free Product campaign, new search and filters mechanism, and finally a new homepage to support the App vision.
dealer.section_key_feature_desc: Through continuous research, analytics, and AB testings, we developed and improved the following functionalities.
dealer.section_key_feature_01: Invite a friend to attract new customers
dealer.section_key_feature_02: Free product to reward our fans
dealer.section_learning_01: Use of analytics and A/B testing
dealer.section_learning_02: Taking full ownership of an App design
dealer.section_learning_03: Manage a basic roadmap of features
dealer.outro: AH Compact was ultimately merged into the large AH App at the end of 2022 due to a change of company strategy. AH Compact has been a fantastic field of experimentation for 2 years, some of its functionalities and styleguide inspired the large App, until now!
assist.title_hero: Ally Assist Virtual Agent Payment Assistance
assist.description_hero: Designed a compassionate chatbot to assist customers who need help understanding options for missed payments.
assist.section_overview_desc: Due to the impact of post-pandemic inflation, 34% of customers need help with either delaying their next few payments or changing the payment contract to reduce their monthly payment (Based on NLP data from Ally Customer Base).
assist.section_context_desc_1: How might we effectively interact with customers who are experiencing financial hardship and are concerned they may miss payments in the next few months?
assist.section_context_desc_3: 1. Reduction in call and chat volumes handled by human associates in our Contact Center.
assist.section_context_desc_4: 2. Reduction in the number of customers going into collections for missing a payment.
assist.section_sketch_desc: Based on the requirements and user research, I sketched the user flow to visualize the conversation design. This helped me identify key touchpoints and potential pain points in the user journey.
assist.section_theming_desc: I mapped the end-to-end user journey, including identifying user intents, possible scenarios and edge cases.
assist.section_multi_desc: The main goal was to understand the level of information users need before committing to the process and to learn if the information is clear to understand to the users.
assist.section_numbers_stat_desc_1: Users felt the information provided throughout the conversation was just right.
assist.section_numbers_stat_desc_2: Users felt certain complex financial terms around payments was unclear.
assist.section_numbers_stat_desc_3: On a scale of 1-5, the users felt the chat messages were educational & compassionate.
assist.section_approach_1: Content design approach 1: Clear but compassionate
assist.section_approach_desc_1: I took the approach to use straightforward language to ensure that the information is easy to understand for users who might be stressed about their financial situations.
assist.section_approach_desc_2: There were technical limitations and security concerns around pulling user data when they haven’t missed their payment, so I added an option to direct user to the internal payment assistance tool to see if they qualify.
assist.section_learning_1: Direct language around payments might be too promissory to users
assist.section_learning_3: Example: can -> might be able to
assist.section_storybook_desc: There were technical limitations and security concerns around pulling user data when they haven’t missed their payment, so I added an option to direct user to the internal payment assistance tool to see if they qualify.
assist.section_next_desc_1: 23% reduction in chat and call volumes
assist.section_next_desc_2: 18% less customers going into collections for missing a payment
assist.section_next_desc_3: Boosted customer’s confidence in discussing their situation with human associates (based on Ally Customer data and survey results from Q1 2025).
women.description_hero: Ahold Delhaize started its Design System with an ambitious goal unite existing initiatives to standardise its design and development efforts to deliver a consistent and high-quality user experiences across all touchpoints.
women.protected_desc: Pantry Design System is an ongoing project in which I am lucky to take part weekly. We are currently focusing on the accessibility, the adoption and the contribution to the system by all product teams. The rest of this content is protected.
women.section_key_results_stat_desc_1: The same codebase for iOS, Android, Flutter & web
women.section_key_results_stat_desc_2: Ensures a perfect alignment between UX, Tech & brands
women.section_key_results_stat_desc_3: in 1 year, fully documented & aligned with development
women.section_context: Context — the need for a Design System
women.section_context_subtitle: What is a design system and why it matters.
women.section_context_desc_1: A design system is a standardized approach to managing design that promotes consistency and eliminates redundancy across various pages and channels.
women.section_context_desc_2: It includes items such as colors, typography, spacing, and UI elements (e.g., buttons, forms, navigation controls) that are clearly defined to ensure product coherence.
women.section_challenges_subtitle01: #1 There is no dedicated design system team
women.section_challenges_desc01: The project started as a design initiative, so it quickly became paramount to convince management to allocate time and budget to keep and scale the project up.
women.section_challenges_approach01: Our approach present the benefits of a design system to management with achievable goals on the short and long term in order to get focus, budget and support.
women.section_challenges_subtitle02: #2 Launch and maintain the system across 4 platforms
women.section_challenges_desc02: The current system is inconsistent between platforms due to a lot of legacy. We need to create the ground for long-term alignment.
women.section_challenges_approach02: Our approach work on the audit, starting with foundations. Map all styles mismatching and make some first hard decisions. Iterate over time.
women.section_challenges_subtitle03: #3 Start from scratch while showing progress
women.section_challenges_desc03: The amount of work ahead was important, but it was also important to show progress not to loose the momentum and the curiosity from the community. our team and efforts to build enthusiasm.
women.section_challenges_approach03: Our approach create channels of communications to showcase monthly effort, progress, and stir up the enthusiasm of the community.
women.section_phase0_desc: The project began by interviewing designers, developers, managers, and product owners about the current system while gathering all available assets and components for our investigation. To stay focused, the team split into two Design streams, each with its own objective
women.section_stream1_task01: Creating a high-level roadmap for the first 6 months
women.section_stream1_task02: Building presentations for higher management to get buy-in
women.section_stream1_task03: Decide on the governance model to structure a winning team
women.section_stream2_task01: Audit of current foundations and components
women.section_stream2_task02: Creating the set of libraries and sandbox files
women.section_stream2_task03: Start creating some draft foundations and components
women.section_audit_desc: We performed an analysis of all the visual and technical elements of our digital products, from websites to Apps. We also looked at famous design systems like Carbon, Material3, Spectrum, and many more. This helped us in finding the right set-up for our organisation. Our audit revealed 3 main insights
women.section_audit_desc_insight01: A lot of inconsistency both in design, and in the code
women.section_audit_desc_insight02: Components with vague definition and overlapping usecases
women.section_audit_desc_insight03: Foundations that are open for interpretation, and not documented
women.section_ambition_desc: One strong statement that would guide all of our decisions along the project.
women.section_phase2_desc: Design tokens are the small, repeatable design decisions that define a system's visual style. They replace static values, like hex codes, with descriptive names. While initially tedious, this approach proves invaluable once the first set of foundations is implemented, offering long-term benefits. Our tokens range from color to line-height, font-family, spacing, sizing, breakpoint and even motion.
women.section_foundations: Foundations — The backbones of the system
women.section_foundations_desc: The tokens let us systemize all of our foundations, from core to semantic values. They all rely on similar naming conventions, and ranged from colors, textstyles, spacing, borderRadius, and more...
women.section_components_official_desc: All components that go through the Design System process, from the request to the design, refinement, building, testing and accessibility checks. They are consisdered as official only once available on all platforms.
women.section_components_beta_desc: These reflect the exact states of the current and existing components present in the code. They didn't go through the Design System process yet, but are available to designers, and monitored for future improvement.
women.section_single_source_desc: To ensure the consistency and increase the adoption of the system, we used zeroheight as the accessible and clear platform to document all our design decisions, processes, and foundations/components.
women.section_phase3_subtitle: There is no sustainable design system without a supporting community and stakeholders. In order to maintain interest and excitment around the system, we introduced
women.section_phase3_task01: A monthly demo, showcasing the latest components and activities of the team
women.section_phase3_task02: A monthly newsletter, recapitulating the main progress
women.section_phase3_task03: A centralized Teams channel to collect and answer all system-related questions
women.section_phase3_task04: An official form collecting all requests of new components
women.section_accessibility_desc: An accessible design system makes it easier for designers to create products with inclusive customer experiences for all users that don’t discriminate our users with disabilities. Besides, as of 28 June 2025, companies must ensure that the newly marketed products and services covered by the Act are accessible. To achieve AA, we provide foundations that support text scaling and high-contrast mode, and components that are Born accessible (touch area, voiceOver, scalable layout, ...).
women.section_mature: How the system continues to mature
women.section_mature_subtitle: A design system is in constant evolution. In the coming time, we expect the team to
women.section_mature_task01: Make the system available to more platforms
women.section_mature_task02: Open and guide other teams to contribute to the system
women.section_mature_task03: Automate the codeGen of all tokens
women.section_learning: What I take away from this project
women.section_learning_1: This project gave me a chance to play at the “tree and forest levels” of the organisation. Overall, I've learned
women.section_learning_2: What it takes to build a design system (almost) from scratch.
women.section_learning_3: The process of creating foundations and components for 4 platforms in a streamlined way.
women.section_learning_4: How important buy-ins from stakeholders are...
women.credits: Kudos to Dominique, Romijn, Joost, Rene, Dave, Michael & Eduardo
google-en.description_hero: CARL is a mobile app that helps casual travelers rent vehicles with maximum clarity. From start to finish, the user has full control over their choice and the extras and can ask for service support at any time.
google-en.section_benchmark_desc: As a first step, I browsed various car rental apps to identify common patterns, best practices, typical user flows, and potential frictions to understand how these services function.
google-en.section_usability_desc: I then interviewed a potential user with a test script to gain insights into their mindset while renting a car.
google-en.section_affinity_desc: Organizing insights into key categories proved essential for creating the journey map. As I arranged sticky notes during a digital workshop on Miro, potential solutions and opportunities emerged.
google-en.section_journey_map_desc: Mapping a persona's user journey highlighted the need for a car rental app that better explains the booking process and guides users in selecting extras and protections.
google-en.section_interaction_desc: Sketching rough iterations of each screen on paper ensured that the elements translated to digital wireframes would effectively address the user pain points.
google-en.section_hifi_prototype_desc: I built the prototype by focusing on the primary flow (booking a car) and experimenting with secondary flows (onboarding, profile, booking tab, and filters). Figma let me create the necessary interactions to test the app myself before involving real users for further testing.
radius.description_hero: There are many ways to tell stories... From watercolor to illustration and animation, I'm experimenting with different ways to visualize my thoughts.
radius.section_coffee_desc: Series of illustration created during my different trips to Montréal, Qc.
radius.section_ratatouille_desc: A story about the 2020 pandemic and cooking...
fitness.description_hero: The Flutter Puzzle Hack 2022 pushed our creativity's limits by letting us reimagine this classic puzzle. Inspired by the Dutch islands and Minecraft, this game lets you rebuild the island if you succeed in completing the game.
fitness.section_gameplay_desc: Inspired by a mix of minecraft blocks and the dutch islands, we gave to this puzzle a friendly-geeky look and feel. After shuffling the game, the numbered tiles change into illustrated ones to complete the fitness. A few flying and floating elements move around to complete the picture.
fitness.section_teamwork_desc: We challenged ourselves with visual effects and transitions (including a few RIVE animations) to improve the game experience, while my teammate Rene was implementing the puzzle for all platforms.
fitness.section_end_game_desc: The full island is revealed once all the blocks are in the right position.
fitness.credits: Project created in collaboration with Rene Floor, Flutter tech lead.
